summary: Streaming graceful-shutdown causes in-flight funcall finalization loss and idempotency ambiguities
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports that during streaming client shutdowns (app crash or SIGTERM during an open stream), some in-flight function/tool calls are not being finalized on their backend webhooks and occasionally re-executed after client reconnects. Impact: duplicate side-effects in customer systems (order confirmations) and uncertainty about whether calls were committed or rolled back. Observed pattern appears correlated with short shutdown windows and clients that rely on SDK graceful-shutdown hooks. Customer expects deterministic at-most-once semantics or clear confirmation tokens to reconcile duplicates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long-running chat generation with an attached funcall to POST /webhook/order-confirm on redwood-2.7-small in us-east-1
2) Trigger a SIGTERM in the client within 200-800ms after the funcall is delivered but before the stream ack is received by the client
3) Restart the client (or reconnect) and resend without an explicit idempotency key in the funcall payload
4) Observe webhook receiving duplicate POSTs or an initial POST with no final confirmation, followed by a replay from the client or platform fallback.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:08:26Z serving-runtime: outbound-webhook POST /webhook/order-confirm status=200 body_digest=sha256:ab12... confirmation_token=tok_f_3e9
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: graceful-shutdown path in SDK closes stream before platform acks are reliably persisted to funcall-confirmation store.
Correlates with short shutdown windows where client does not wait for final confirmation frame over the stream (observed on both Go and Python SDKs).

Serving runtime shows outbound webhook returned 200 and confirmation_token generated, but client did not receive the final confirmation frame before disconnect. Platform replay logic then re-enqueued the funcall because confirmation metadata was not yet durable in the request ledger at time of disconnect.

Possible contributing factor: write ordering between webhook confirmation persistence and stream frame push; if persistence is async and ack frame send is raced with client disconnect, we can observe "unconfirmed_ack" state.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1893 addresses making confirmation write synchronous (experiment branch).
Telemetry: increased incidence when dedicated GPU pools experience GC/eviction events and when clients use SDK shutdown-timeout < 1s.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Jordan Lee (Support): Logged with BrightCart CSM Anna Patel. They reproduced locally with Go SDK v1.4.2 and Python SDK v1.6.0; provided request/trace IDs. Requested immediate mitigation guidance.

2026-03-10 16:10 - Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Confirmed trace shows outbound webhook succeeded before replay. Filing hypothesis that persistence ordering is the gap. Spinning a reproducible test harness to force window races.

2026-03-11 09:17 - BrightCart (Anna Patel): Workaround tested: client waits for confirmation_token frame up to 3s before shutdown -> duplicates gone in our trials, but unacceptable latency for some flows.

2026-03-11 11:30 - Rafael Ortiz (SRE): Added a short-term mitigation: instructing dedicated clusters to enable 'sync-confirmation-write' feature-flag. Patch rollout planned to a subset of BrightCart's dedicated pool TOMORROW morning.

2026-03-11 14:00 - Dev (Priya Nair): Noted potential performance cost for sync writes; proposing a hybrid approach: persist minimal confirmation stub before sending frame and confirm full metadata in background with idempotent replay suppression.

2026-03-12 08:45 - Jordan Lee (Support): Communicated planned rollout and recommended SDK guidance to add client-side confirmation wait with configurable timeout. Customer acknowledged and requested follow-up to evaluate long-term solution.
resolution: In Progress: short-term mitigation (feature-flag to make confirmation persistence synchronous) scheduled for canary on BrightCart's dedicated pool. Customer advised to add a client-side confirmation wait of up to 3s as a stopgap. Long-term design work underway to implement a hybrid 'stub-first' confirmation write + idempotent replay suppression to avoid latency regressions.
recommended_workaround: Client-side: after receiving funcall.delivery event, block shutdown for up to configurable timeout (default 3000ms) waiting for funcall.confirmation frame. Server-side: enable feature-flag 'sync-confirmation-write' on dedicated pools to ensure confirmation durability before stream frame is considered committed.
follow_up_actions: 1) SRE to canary 'sync-confirmation-write' flag on BrightCart dedicated pool (owner: Rafael Ortiz)
2) SDK team to publish guidance snippet and small helper that exposes 'await_confirmation(timeout_ms=...)' in Go/Python/TS SDKs (owner: Priya Nair)
3) Eng to design hybrid persistence approach and open RFC (owner: Priya Nair)
4) CS to monitor BrightCart for duplicate webhook events for 72 hours post-canary (owner: Jordan Lee)
